explanation: ignored_alert.xml under rationalVault/reqlin_xml/ (the Linux template directory) contains the wrong schema -- it has the 8-tag Windows schema (security_drift, user_breach, unknown_binary, registry_drift, hostfile_modified, temp_execution, suspicious_commands, network_anamoly) instead of the 22-tag Linux schema that Ignore_Events_Alert.sh actually reads (which includes DBmod, dbrans, ssh_key_injection, drop_table, etc.). Any lookup against this file for a Linux hierarchy is reading the wrong template -- most of the 22 tags Ignore_Events_Alert.sh checks won't exist in it at all.

metadata.caveat: CRITICAL -- do not treat missing tags in this file as 'not detected'; the schema itself is wrong for Linux
metadata.raw_content_example:
<!-- what this file ACTUALLY contains on a Linux hierarchy (wrong -- this is the Windows schema): -->
<user_response>
  <security_drift>0</security_drift>
  <registry_drift>0</registry_drift>
  <hostfile_modified>0</hostfile_modified>
  <temp_execution>0</temp_execution>
</user_response>

<!-- what Ignore_Events_Alert.sh actually looks for (a sample of the real 22 Linux tags -- these keys don't exist above): -->
<!-- DBmod, dbrans, ssh_key_injection, drop_table, log_tampering, honeypot, ... -->
metadata.raw_content_note: the top block is the real, verified content of the deployed Linux template; the bottom is what the consuming script expects -- the mismatch itself, shown side by side, is the bug
